test_title: PYST 14: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 11 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What was the life expectancy at birth in India as per the 2021 World Health Organization data?
solution:
The correct answer is __**67.3 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the 2021 World Health Organization (WHO) data, the life expectancy at birth in India was **67.3 years**.
 
• Life expectancy at birth is a measure indicating the average number of years a newborn is expected to live under current mortality rates.
 
• India's life expectancy has shown a gradual increase over the years but still lags behind the global average of approximately **73 years**.
 
• Factors such as improved healthcare services, better sanitation, and vaccination programs have contributed to the rise in life expectancy in India.
 
• Despite progress, challenges such as high infant mortality rates and unequal access to healthcare services persist.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Life Expectancy:**

 
 
• As of 2021, the global average life expectancy at birth is estimated to be **73.4 years** (WHO).
 
• Japan has one of the highest life expectancies globally at approximately **84 years**.
 
 
 
• **Factors Influencing Life Expectancy:**
 
 
• Life expectancy is influenced by access to healthcare, nutrition, sanitation, and socioeconomic conditions.
 
• Public health policies, vaccination drives, and improvements in maternal and child health significantly impact life expectancy.
 
 
 
• **India’s Healthcare Challenges:**
 
 
• India faces disparities in healthcare access between urban and rural areas.
 
• Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) like diabetes and heart diseases are rising concerns, affecting life expectancy.
 
 
 
• **Infant Mortality Rate (IMR):**
 
 
• IMR is a critical indicator of a country's healthcare system and directly affects life expectancy.
 
• India's IMR has declined over the years, standing at **27 deaths per 1,000 live births** as per 2021 data.
